subsystems.name: Air mover
subsystems.role: pulls ambient air in and pushes cleaned air toward the nose and mouth.

subsystems.name: Filter media
parts: activated carbon layer for gases and odours

subsystems.name: Electrostatic stage
subsystems.role: gives particles a charge so they stick to plates instead of passing through.

subsystems.name: Power and control
subsystems.role: runs the fans, electrodes and sensors from a battery.

subsystems.name: Sensing
subsystems.role: measures how dirty the surrounding air is and adjusts output.

subsystems.name: Delivery interface
subsystems.role: the part that decides how much cleaned air actually reaches the user's airway.

buildSteps.title: Set a performance target
buildSteps.detail: Decide how much particle reduction is needed in the breathing zone and the airflow to achieve it, in litres per minute.

buildSteps.title: Make the filter media
buildSteps.detail: Polypropylene fibres are melt-blown to sub-micrometre diameters, given an electrostatic charge so they capture particles by attraction as well as by sieving, then pleated to add area.

buildSteps.title: Build the electrostatic stage
buildSteps.detail: Electrodes and collection plates are stamped and assembled, and a small high-voltage circuit is added; ozone production must be held near zero.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the air path
buildSteps.detail: Fans, filter, electrodes and ducts are fitted into a housing designed to keep airflow smooth and noise low.

buildSteps.title: Add electronics
buildSteps.detail: Battery, charging circuit, particle sensor and control firmware are installed and calibrated against reference aerosols.

buildSteps.title: Shape the wearable
buildSteps.detail: The shell is moulded in lightweight plastic to sit comfortably on the neck or head, with the outlet aimed at the nose and mouth.

buildSteps.title: Test in a chamber
buildSteps.detail: A person or breathing mannequin sits in a chamber filled with a known aerosol while particle counters compare inhaled air with room air; leakage and comfort are also measured.

prerequisites.why: the same material class used in respirators and HVAC filters, but at a small, low-power scale.

prerequisites.tech: Miniature brushless fans and lithium batteries
prerequisites.why: quiet fans and small cells make a wearable air path possible at all.
they let the device react to real pollution instead of running at fixed output.

prerequisites.tech: A test standard for personal clean-air delivery
prerequisites.why: there is no agreed method to certify how much a wearable actually reduces what a person inhales.

pathway.milestone: neck- and head-worn purifiers sold mainly in Asian markets, some with a visor feeding filtered air to the face
pathway.unlocks: a personal option where outdoor air is heavily polluted.

pathway.milestone: independent chamber testing and a comparable performance rating
pathway.unlocks: buyers can tell a real reduction in inhaled particles from a marketing claim.

pathway.milestone: quieter, lighter designs integrated with headphones or a light mask
pathway.unlocks: devices people actually wear all day.

pathway.milestone: adaptive systems that sense the wearer's breathing and the local pollution and deliver air only when needed
pathway.unlocks: longer battery life and better protection during commutes and wildfire smoke.
